The cautious hiker checked the ice before stepping.
The wooden dock began to deteriorate after years of rain.
The class built an elaborate model of the river town.
A frigid wind crossed the field at sunrise.
Her genuine thanks made the volunteer smile.
He did not hesitate to share his umbrella.
An immense oak shaded the whole playground.

vocabulary.meaning: free time for rest or play
vocabulary.example: They spent their leisure reading on the porch.

vocabulary.meaning: to move from one region to another
vocabulary.example: The geese migrate south when the days grow short.

vocabulary.meaning: to care for so something can grow
vocabulary.example: Gardeners nurture seedlings until they can stand alone.
A fallen tree was the only obstacle on the trail.
The map gave precise directions to the bridge.
The reluctant cat finally came in from the rain.
Fresh berries were scarce after the dry week.

vocabulary.meaning: bright, clear, and full of life
vocabulary.example: She told a vivid story about the night market.

grammar.prompt: The box of pencils (sit / sits) on the top shelf.
Yesterday the team (practice / practiced) until dusk.
Maya forgot (her / their) lunch on the bus.
Add the missing commas: We packed apples cheese crackers and juice.
grammar.answer: We packed apples, cheese, crackers, and juice.

grammar.prompt: Join the sentences with because: The trail was muddy. It had rained all night.
grammar.answer: The trail was muddy because it had rained all night.

grammar.prompt: This path is (more steeper / steeper) than the last one.
Rewrite so the sentence is clear: I don't have no pencil.

passages.title: The creek after rain
passages.text: Maya reached the creek and stopped. The stones she usually crossed were under brown water. She walked upstream to the footbridge instead, even though it made her late.
passages.question: Why did Maya use the footbridge?

passages.title: Market morning
passages.text: Before the shops opened, Mr. Alvarez set out crates of oranges. A boy counted them in tens while his sister wrote the number on a card. When the first customer arrived, the card already said 80.
passages.question: How did the children keep track of the oranges?
passages.answer: They counted in tens and wrote the number on a card.

passages.title: Library window
passages.text: Jonah chose a table by the window so he could watch the storm. He finished his notes before the rain stopped. On the way home he kept the notebook under his coat.
passages.question: Why did Jonah put the notebook under his coat?
passages.answer: He was protecting it from the rain.

passages.title: The nest
passages.text: A pair of robins built a nest in the school garden. Students walked around the bush instead of through it. By Friday, three blue eggs were visible from the path.
passages.question: How did the students protect the nest?

passages.title: Practice
passages.text: Lena's first serve went into the net. She bounced the ball twice, looked at the service line, and tried again. The second serve landed just inside the box.
passages.question: What changed between Lena's two serves?
passages.answer: The second serve landed inside the box.

passages.title: Night shift
passages.text: The lighthouse keeper checked the lamp at dusk and again at midnight. Ships could see the beam from far out on the water. He wrote both times in the log before he slept.
passages.question: Why did the keeper check the lamp twice?
passages.answer: So ships could see the beam through the night.

readings.text: The tomato plants were abundant after the warm week. Baskets filled faster than the family could carry them. They shared the extra fruit with neighbors.
readings.question: What did the family do with the extra tomatoes?

readings.text: A cautious fox waited at the edge of the road. Two cars passed before it crossed. Then it slipped into the tall grass.
readings.question: What did the fox do before it crossed?

readings.text: The rope bridge began to deteriorate after the flood. Boards split, and the ropes grew thin. The town closed the bridge until it was repaired.
readings.question: Why did the town close the bridge?

readings.text: The science project was elaborate. It had moving parts, small labels, and a painted river. Judges stayed at that table for a long time.
readings.question: Why did the judges stay so long?
readings.answer: The project had many detailed parts.

readings.text: The morning was frigid, and the pond wore a skin of ice. Students kept gloves on at the bus stop. Their breath showed in the air.
readings.question: What showed that the morning was frigid?
readings.answer: The pond was icy and their breath showed.

readings.text: Sam wrote a genuine thank-you note instead of copying one. He named the exact help his uncle had given. His uncle put the note on the fridge.
readings.question: How was Sam's note different from a copied note?
readings.answer: He named the exact help he received.

readings.text: When the teacher asked for a volunteer, Priya did not hesitate. Her hand went up, and she walked to the board. The class grew quiet.
readings.question: What did Priya do when the teacher asked?

readings.text: An immense cloud crossed the sun during recess. Its shadow covered the whole field. The bright afternoon turned dim in a moment.
readings.question: How large was the cloud's shadow?

readings.text: Saturday was for leisure. No homework sat on the table, and the bikes were ready. They rode to the creek and stayed until lunch.
readings.question: How did they spend their free time?
readings.answer: They rode bikes to the creek.

readings.text: The geese migrate when the nights turn cold. Their line crossed town just after dawn. Students counted the birds from the classroom window.
readings.question: When do the geese leave in this passage?

readings.text: Club members nurture the garden all spring. They water, weed, and cover young plants on cold nights. By June the beds are full.
readings.question: What three jobs protect the young plants?

readings.text: A fallen log was an obstacle on the trail. The hikers could not step over it. They pushed through the brush beside the path.
readings.question: How did the hikers get past the log?
readings.answer: They went through the brush beside it.

readings.text: The map was precise. It said to turn at the red barn and count three mailboxes. The group found the lane without guessing.
readings.question: Why did the group not have to guess?
readings.answer: The map told them the barn and the mailboxes.

readings.text: The reluctant swimmer stayed on the last step. The water looked cold, and a friend waited in the pool. After a long pause, she went in.
readings.question: What kept the swimmer on the step at first?

readings.text: Rain was scarce that month. The creek shrank to a narrow thread. Gardens took water from barrels beside the shed.
readings.question: Where did the gardens get water?

readings.text: Her vivid story made the market easy to picture. She named the colors of the spices and the sound of the drums. Listeners could almost smell the bread.
readings.question: Which senses did the story use?
